primitives.verbatim_quote: GSE lens - **Self-knowledge distillation as a compression doctrine:** bge-m3's public recipe distills the three retrieval modes into one model so a single forward pass serves all three.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M': 'model architecture (XLM-RoBERTa)', 'R_d': 'dense retrieval mode output vector', 'R_s': 'sparse retrieval mode output weights', 'R_m': 'multi-vector retrieval mode output vectors'}

primitives.name: Three Retrieval Modes
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision One embedding model that does three retrieval jobs at once: dense embeddings (single vector), sparse lexical weights (SPLADE-style term weights), and multi-vector ColBERT-style token embeddings — plus 100+ language support and 8K context.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_d': 'dense embedding vector ∈ ℝ^d', 'W_s': 'sparse weight vector ∈ ℝ^n', 'V_m': 'multi-vector token embeddings ∈ ℝ^(k×t)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each mode captures different aspects of semantic structure; modes are orthogonal in information content.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When input domain shifts beyond training distribution of any single mode.

layer2.mapping: Kernel functions derived from each mode define similarity metrics in respective embedding spaces.
layer2.telemetry: Per-mode recall@K performance on benchmark datasets.

reasoning_traces.think:
bge-m3 embodies a dual duality: it simultaneously encodes dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval semantics within a single transformer backbone. This is achieved via shared attention layers and distinct output heads, where each head produces a different type of embedding. The self-distillation mechanism ensures that these outputs remain coherent and aligned, forming a compact yet expressive representation. The failure mode occurs when the semantic differences between retrieval modes exceed the model’s capacity to encode them coherently. In such cases, the model may collapse into a single dominant mode, losing discriminative power across retrieval types. The architecture supports a principled approach to signal fusion in GSI by allowing multiple views of the same data to be processed concurrently, enabling robust Bayesian inference over uncertain signals.
